summary.en-US: Translate Netflix and Prime Video subtitles locally using your own Ollama models.

description.en-US:
LST — Local Subtitle Translate adds locally generated translations to Netflix and Prime Video subtitles.

LST connects to an Ollama server running on your computer by default and lets you choose or download a model. DeepSeek and Gemini are also available as optional providers when you supply your own API key. Subtitle translation can happen in real time, or an episode can be precomputed and cached before playback.

Features:

• Local Ollama translation with TranslateGemma 4B as the default model
• Optional DeepSeek and Gemini translation providers
• Installed-model selection and model downloads
• Real-time subtitle translation
• Full-track precomputation and automatic look-ahead caching
• Local translation cache with provider and per-episode storage management
• Independent service, original, and translated subtitle visibility
• Customizable subtitle placement, sizing, and timing
• Persistent in-player status and quick-settings pill
• Tabbed settings navigation
• Advanced translation prompt editor with restore-original control
• Per-service switches, so either service can be turned off on its own
• Configurable position for the in-player LST control
• Idle behavior on browse, Home, and storefront pages
• Optional status messages and detailed diagnostics
• Subtitles imported for an episode the service does not subtitle, either from Jimaku or from a subtitle file you already have
• The player says where its subtitles come from: an imported file is marked in the in-player controls, and a note about what Jimaku holds for a show is shown when you open another episode of it — read from your own device, never looked up because a page was opened
• An imported file already in your target language is shown without translating anything
• Optional per-service switches and an in-player control position

LST does not require a cloud translation service. By default, subtitle text is sent only to Ollama running at http://localhost:11434. If you select DeepSeek or Gemini, subtitle text is sent directly to that provider using your API key and may be subject to its terms, privacy policy, quota, or charges. LST has no developer-operated translation, analytics, or telemetry service.

Developer comments

I built LST after moving to Japan and running into a surprisingly common problem: a lot of anime available here only includes Japanese subtitles. LST started as a way to make those shows easier to follow by translating subtitles locally with my own Ollama models instead of relying on a cloud translation service. A compatible Ollama installation and at least one installed model are required when using the local provider. Netflix gets full-track capture, so an episode can be precomputed and cached. Prime Video currently runs on the realtime path: LST reads the caption line the player draws and translates it as it appears, and does not yet offer precompute or a transcript sidebar there unless you import a subtitle file for the episode, which gives it a full track. A subtitle file you already have on your own computer can be imported the same way, and that path makes no network request at all. Importing is optional: LST asks for access to jimaku.cc and www.subtitlebot.com only when you press Search in the import card, and never contacts them otherwise. LST supports Netflix and Prime Video on the hosts listed in its manifest and is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by Netflix or Amazon.

version.approval_notes: LST translates Netflix and Prime Video subtitle text through a user-selected provider. Ollama defaults to localhost:11434; DeepSeek and Gemini are optional and require user-supplied API keys. The extension observes timed-text fetch/XHR responses to parse TTML or WebVTT and falls back to the rendered subtitle DOM. Prime Video ships on the rendered-caption path and adds no host permission: capture happens in the page world, and the extension refuses to read a tab's URL so no tabs or Amazon host permission is requested. Provider keys remain in browser extension storage and are not sent to Netflix pages or diagnostics. Subtitle import is the only other network access and is entirely user-initiated: the two hosts (jimaku.cc and www.subtitlebot.com) are optional_host_permissions requested when the viewer presses Search, never granted at install or on upgrade; a supplied Jimaku API key is stored like a provider key; and a URL that leaves jimaku.cc is refused rather than fetched. There is no telemetry, analytics, advertising, tracking, remote executable code, or developer-operated backend. The submitted source is readable vanilla JavaScript, HTML, and CSS with no build or minification step. Full testing instructions are included in AMO_REVIEWER_NOTES.md in the source repository.
